key_insight: SemantEq tests faithful statement equivalence through allowed transformations, avoiding ordinary logical equivalence that can link unrelated provable statements.
engineering_relevance: Separating proof generation from proof acceptance lets stronger provers improve coverage without weakening checks on autoformalized mathematics.
method: Require transformations in both directions using allowed steps such as logical rearrangement and library-equation rewriting.
Search for admissible equivalence proofs with SemantEq-Eval.
Audit model-generated Lean proof terms—not tactic scripts—with SemantEq-ProofAudit.
evidence_signal: On the adjudicated ProofNetVerif test split, SemantEq-Eval achieved 100% precision and 65.6% recall versus BEq+'s 95.8% and 61.8%; under the best prompt, ProofAudit raised recall from 65.4% to 81.1% on 407 equivalent pairs while accepting none of 104 non-equivalent pairs.
watch_item: Results are benchmark-specific, and faithful reformulations outside the allowed transformation policy may be rejected.
paper_title: SemantEq: Faithful Bidirectional Equivalence of Formal Statements
